name: Two-Obstruction PC-Minor Basis for Median Graphs
statement: A finite partial cube is median if and only if it has no pc-minor isomorphic to $Q_3^-$ or $C_6$. Both listed graphs are nonmedian and all of their proper pc-minors are median.
proof: The avoidance equivalence is the cited two-obstruction theorem. The graph $Q_3^-$ fails majority closure at the three neighbors of its missing vertex, while $C_6$ has triples with no common interval vertex. Their elementary proper projections, conditionings, and $\Theta$-class contractions are cubes, paths, or four-cycles, hence median; the same then holds for every further proper pc-minor.
